title: P2.15d-i Land a daemon-owned approval intent seam so the Control Room can approve a plan without caller-shaped authority bytes
description:
Leaf carved out of task-40017f79 (P2.15d) by architect-ac8532da on 2026-08-27 at HEAD fa0736e3. THE GAP, measured: the only plan-approval command is `approval.decide`, whose exact payload roster is `["activation", "command", "graphRevisionRef", "record", "runId"]` (apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:196) and whose handler `intentOf` (apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-graph-approve.ts:81-95) REQUIRES the caller to supply the `activation` object (activationRef, expectedGoalVersion, graphHash, policyHash, qualityHash, `truthClass: "HUMAN_APPROVED"`), the `command` object (decision, decisionReason, stepUpAuthRef…) and the `record` object — i.e. the caller authors the activation witness and the approval record. The human grant itself is minted server-side from a `HumanReviewWitness` (`operatorReviewAuthority` :58-70, `grantHumanAuthority({kind:"HUMAN", principalId: witness.principalId}, …)`), so the PRINCIPAL is honest, but the activation/record bytes are caller-shaped. The Control Room's only payload for it is `DEV_PAYLOADS["approval.decide"]` (apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch.ts:185-195), explicitly fixture-shaped (`hex64("6a")` hashes, `"activation-1"`), and the approve screen is deliberately disabled with a "no fabricated decision" note (apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.tsx:41-50; pinned by tests/e2e/control-room/prd-to-approval.spec.ts:127-128). P2.15d's task rail forbids treating a caller-shaped HUMAN flag or enabled button as approval authority, so the UI cannot be wired to this command as it stands (architect-be964894 reached the same conclusion on 08-25, comment-9810f791).

WHAT THIS LEAF LANDS: a daemon-owned seam where the caller supplies ONLY intent — `{ runId, decision: "APPROVE" | "REJECT", decisionReason }` — and the daemon derives the activation witness (graph/policy/quality hashes, expectedGoalVersion, truthClass) and the approval record from the DURABLE run in PLAN_REVIEW (the sealed plan the planning-run read already serves, apps/control-room/src/live/live-planning-run.ts:322 over POST /planning/run/read) and from the authenticated operator session, then commits through the existing approval edge so the core `applyApprovalCommand`/`decideApprovalAuthority` path is unchanged. Two designs to choose between at planning, measured symbol by symbol: (A) a NEW runtime command kind (e.g. `approval.decide_intent`) — carries the five-file generated fan-out (runtime-vocabulary.ts frozen tuple, runtime-contract.test.ts literal count, stdio-schemas injectivity, regenerated control-room-client + goldens, release-subject digest mirrors; precedent task-ad61563a / 5ff4e396), or (B) a second exact payload shape admitted by the daemon for the EXISTING kind (a shape switch on the exact key roster: full shape for existing callers, intent shape derived server-side) — no generated fan-out, but the vocabulary test's PAYLOAD_KEYS roster and the registry/security arms that enumerate exact rosters must be traced (rail 7B). Whichever is chosen, hostile arms must pin: a caller-supplied `activation`/`record` beside intent refuses at the exact-shape fence; an AGENT session refuses `APPROVAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED`/the core human-authority tuple verbatim; a run not in PLAN_REVIEW refuses the run-state code; replay is the ledger's answer. Consumer: task-40017f79 (P2.15d) wires the Control Room approve button to this seam, affordance-gated.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK on disk: `approval.decide` PAYLOAD_KEYS at daemon-command-vocabulary.ts still require `activation` and `record` (else the seam exists — duplicate, report blocked); `intentOf` at daemon-command-graph-approve.ts still reads them from the caller payload; no daemon file admits an intent-only approval shape; porcelain of the daemon command files you will touch is clean or carries only your hunks; the design choice (new kind vs second shape) is recorded with its measured fan-out set before any edit.

A daemon-owned seam admits EXACTLY `{ runId, decision, decisionReason }` (plus the session presentation if the existing witness path requires one — measure how `humanReview` reaches the registry), derives activation witness and record from the durable PLAN_REVIEW run and the authenticated operator, and commits through the existing approval edge; the caller cannot supply `activation`, `record`, `truthClass`, hashes, `stepUpAuthRef` or any principal/time — each extra key refuses at the exact-shape fence with the stable code and stage, asserted over a nonzero generated roster.

Refusals carry exact code AND layer verbatim: AGENT/non-operator session → the core/daemon human-authority tuple unchanged; run absent or not in PLAN_REVIEW → the run-state code; graph revision mismatch → the existing graph code; replay → the ledger's stored decision without a second event; conflicting retry → the ledger's bytes-conflict tuple.

If a new RUNTIME_COMMAND_KIND is introduced, all generated artifacts and digest mirrors are declared owned paths and regenerated (never hand-edited) in the same commit and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test` passes with a nonzero count; if not, a row comment says so explicitly and the vocabulary/registry/security roster arms that enumerate exact payload rosters are updated in both directions.

Focused daemon suites run standalone with nonzero counts (`pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json <owned tests>`), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exits 0 with its `$ tsc` echo; drills red a named arm each: honour a caller `activation` → the shape-fence roster arm; skip the PLAN_REVIEW check → the run-state arm; mint the grant from a payload principal → the AGENT arm. Every production file ≤ 400 lines (split before); explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names task-40017f79 as the consumer.
taskRails: Human authority is not delegable: the daemon derives witness, record and grant from durable state and the authenticated session; the caller supplies intent only.
Do not enable or reshape DEV_PAYLOADS in the Control Room here; do not edit Control Room files (task-40017f79 owns the UI half).
Trace rail 7B fan-out before choosing a new command kind; explicit-pathspec commits only; preserve foreign WIP.

STEP 1 — VERIFY-OR-BLOCK GATE (read-only; author no bytes). Record with moe.add_comment — the completion summary is write-only and persists nowhere. Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it beside every grep, each UNPIPED with its own exit code and a positive control.

READ THIS FIRST — THIS ROW AND task-ba102165 WERE A CYCLE, AND THIS ROW IS THE BREAK. task-ba1021652dcc4469bc4deb04a8e7d7d5 (durable riskTier + run-linked applicablePolicyRef) is BLOCKED, and its block reason names this row as the reason: "neither daemon-command-graph-approve.ts nor planning-services.ts composes an ApprovalDecisionRecord after decideApprovalAuthority. Both consume a caller-shaped record BEFORE authority and forward it to activation... the missing daemon-owned seam is already owned by blocked consumer task-6646f888. Adding only the planned producer would be an orphan." Meanwhile this row was blocked waiting on that producer's durable sources.
THE RESOLUTION, and it is an ordering not a compromise: THIS ROW LANDS FIRST. It creates the daemon-owned composition site. Until that site exists there is nowhere for a durable tier or policy ref to be composed INTO, which is exactly why the producer would have been an orphan. Do NOT wait on ba102165 and do NOT re-block on it.
HOW THIS ROW SURVIVES THE MISSING TIER HONESTLY: where the record needs a fact that has no durable source yet, the seam REFUSES with a stable code naming the missing fact — it does not default one and it does not accept one from the caller. ba102165 then makes that fact available and the refusal stops firing. Absence and a defaulted value are different answers, and the tier in particular decides whether step-up human authority is required (`approval-invalidation.ts:73` special-cases R3), so a defaulted tier would silently decide an authority question. Record in your step note WHICH facts you had to refuse on — that list is what ba102165 consumes next.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 2 — RED FIRST, ON THE PRODUCTION SURFACE. Do not write the seam yet.

Write the arms that pin what a daemon-owned intent seam must do, and watch each fail against today's caller-shaped path.
(1) INTENT ONLY: a request carrying EXACTLY `{runId, decision, decisionReason}` (plus the session presentation step 1(d) measured, if the witness route requires one) is admitted. Today the path demands `activation` and `record` from the payload, so this reds on a missing-key refusal — quote it; it is the reproduction.
(2) CALLER AUTHORITY IS REFUSED, and this is the row's whole point (task rail 1: "Human authority is not delegable"). A request that supplies its own `activation` or its own `record` is REFUSED with an exact stable code AND the refusing layer, both asserted. Today it is HONOURED — that inversion is the defect.
(3) THE WITNESS AND RECORD ARE DERIVED FROM DURABLE STATE: assert the composed record's fields trace to the durable PLAN_REVIEW run and the authenticated session, not to any caller-supplied value.
(4) REFUSALS CARRY THE EXISTING VOCABULARY VERBATIM (DoD-3), each asserting code AND layer: an AGENT or non-operator session -> the core/daemon human-authority tuple UNCHANGED; a run absent or not in PLAN_REVIEW -> the existing run-state code; a graph revision mismatch -> the existing graph code; a replay -> the ledger's stored decision. Do NOT invent a local vocabulary for any of these — forward what the existing layers already emit.
(5) THE MISSING-FACT REFUSAL from step 1: where the record needs a fact with no durable source, assert the seam refuses naming that fact, with an exact code and layer. This arm is what ba102165 will later flip from refusing to succeeding, so name it clearly enough that the next row can find it.

BEFORE CHOOSING ANY NEW REFUSAL CODE, grep the runtime error registry for which codes admit the aggregate this seam uses. `createRuntimeError` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-error-factory.ts:93-104) returns `UNKNOWN_ERROR` and DOES NOT THROW when the code is unknown or the descriptor does not list the aggregate — a wrong code compiles, runs, refuses, and silently loses its identity while every "it refused" arm stays green. Add a dedicated arm asserting no refusal this seam produces has code `UNKNOWN_ERROR`.

Run standalone, FOREGROUND, UNPIPED: `pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json apps/daemon/src/planning`. The root vitest include has NO `apps/**`, so a bare `pnpm test` runs ZERO daemon tests. Quote every red with its count line.
implementationPlan.note:
RED FIRST — both reds captured, standalone, foreground, unpiped.

RED 1 (the suite): `pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-intent.test.ts` EXIT=1 —
  "Error: Cannot find module './approval-intent.js' imported from .../approval-intent.test.ts"
  "Test Files  1 failed (1)" / "Tests  no tests". The seam does not exist; that IS the gap.

RED 2 (the reproduction on TODAY'S production surface): a throwaway probe sent the exact intent-only payload {decision, decisionReason, runId} to the SHIPPED `approval.decide` through the production `send()` pipeline, on a store driven to PLAN_REVIEW by `driveThrough(store, "approval.decide")`. Outcome verbatim:
  {"advisoryOnly":true,"authority":"NONE","code":"BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID","error":null,"kind":"approval.decide","ok":false,"refusedBy":"DAEMON_INGRESS"}
  "Test Files 1 failed (1)" / "Tests 1 failed (1)", EXIT=1. Probe deleted in the same step; `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/planning/` shows no `__intent-repro` path.
This is the inversion the row removes: the shipped path DEMANDS `activation` and `record` from the caller and refuses intent alone.

ARMS WRITTEN (apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-intent.test.ts, 5 describes):
(1) intent-only is admitted PAST THE SHAPE FENCE — asserted narrowly as "not APPROVAL_INTENT_SHAPE_INVALID", because four record facts have no durable producer yet so success is unreachable and asserting it would be dishonest.
(2) caller `activation` and caller `record` each refused APPROVAL_INTENT_SHAPE_INVALID @ DAEMON_APPROVAL_INTENT, in SEPARATE arms (one degree of freedom each) — plus a generated sweep over 18 authority-bearing extra keys with the denominator PINNED (`expect(forbidden.length).toBe(18)`) so a zero-case sweep cannot pass, and a second sweep over every OMITTED intent key with a nonzero-count assertion.
(3) derivation traced to durable state: exactRevisionHash === run state `submissionHash`, planQualityAssessmentRef === `sealedHashes.qualityHash`, criteriaRef === the sealed-bodies event's `criteriaDigest` (selected BY TYPE, not index), graphRevisionRef === the run's own. Every expected value is READ from the durable record, never restated in the test.
(4) existing vocabulary forwarded verbatim: witness-less dispatch -> APPROVAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED @ APPROVAL_POLICY; foreign-principal witness -> same tuple; unknown run -> BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE; run short of PLAN_REVIEW -> APPROVAL_RUN_NOT_REVIEWABLE @ APPROVAL_RUN_BINDING.
(5) missing-fact refusal -> APPROVAL_INTENT_RISK_TIER_UNAVAILABLE @ DAEMON_APPROVAL_INTENT, plus a roster arm pinning one code per fact (BUDGET_REF / POLICY_REF / RISK_TIER / STEP_UP).
Plus the dedicated anti-UNKNOWN_ERROR arm over five probe shapes.

DIVERGENCE FIXTURE (epic rail 7A), stated in the file header. `bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:34-35` sets MOE_APPROVAL_MODE=SPEED with a stated zero delay, so `decideApprovalAuthority` returns PROCEED for a gate-free run and the POLICY cannot be what refuses a witness-less request. Under SPEED this seam's own human-witness fence is the ONLY mechanism that can answer the AGENT arm — loosen it by one and that arm goes green with nothing else noticing. Under REQUIRE_HUMAN the policy would emit the same tuple and the arm would prove only that the SYSTEM refuses, not that THIS seam refuses.

REFUSAL-CODE REGISTRY CHECK: `refuse` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:240-255) takes a free `code: string` and does NOT route through `createRuntimeError`, so this seam's four own codes cannot degrade to UNKNOWN_ERROR. The anti-UNKNOWN_ERROR arm still guards the FORWARDED core/authority refusals, which do go through the factory.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 3 — THE SEAM. New `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-intent.ts` (<=250 lines) PLUS its `.js` bridge — this tree uses bridges beside every module and a missing one is invisible to tsc and vitest while redding unrelated files at runtime.

THE CONTRACT: admit EXACTLY `{runId, decision, decisionReason}` (plus the session presentation measured in step 1(d) if the witness route requires it) as an EXACT-KEY admission — a fourth key is REFUSED, never trimmed. Trimming is how caller-chosen authority gets in, and this seam exists precisely to stop that.

DERIVE, NEVER ACCEPT (task rail 1, and the DoD's central clause):
- the ACTIVATION WITNESS and the APPROVAL RECORD from the durable PLAN_REVIEW run read out of the store;
- the HUMAN GRANT from the authenticated session, by the route step 1(d) measured — through `decideApprovalAuthority`, which consults the gate FIRST by construction (packages/core/src/planning/approval-policy.ts:127-137) and returns `checkHumanAuthority`'s refusal verbatim. Never `checkHumanAuthority` directly: it is deliberately unpublished from the core barrel (packages/core/src/index.ts:239) and core exposes a single `exports` subpath, so a deep import fails TS6059.
The caller supplies INTENT ONLY. If any field the record needs cannot be derived from durable state or the session, REFUSE naming that field — do not default it and do not fall back to the caller's value.

COMPOSE THE EXISTING AUTHORITY PIECES, never reimplement them: the two production precedents are `daemon-command-graph-approve.ts:125-137` and `planning-services.ts:263-281`. A second human-authority path is a competing authority and is forbidden.

DO NOT TOUCH `daemon-command-graph-approve.ts` in this step. This row lands a NEW seam; retiring the old caller-shaped `intentOf` path is a separate concern and touching it here would put this row's change inside a file whose current behaviour other arms still assert. If your measurement says the two cannot coexist, STOP and report rather than editing it.

Re-run step 2: arms (1), (3), (4), (5) go green against the new seam. Arm (2) may still be red if the OLD path remains reachable — that is step 4's wiring.
implementationPlan.note:
THE SEAM LANDS. `pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-intent.test.ts` -> EXIT=0, "Test Files 1 passed (1)" / "Tests 16 passed (16)". `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` -> EXIT=0 with its `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo.

SPLIT INTO TWO PRODUCTION SOURCES (epic rail 6). The single file measured 318 lines, over the 250 target, so it split on a real responsibility line, not an arbitrary one: `approval-intent-sources.ts` (146) answers "what does the store already know about this run"; `approval-intent.ts` (201) answers "may this principal approve, and can a record be composed". Each carries its `.js` bridge — a missing bridge is invisible to tsc and vitest while redding unrelated files at runtime.

CONTRACT: `APPROVAL_INTENT_PAYLOAD_KEYS = ["decision","decisionReason","runId"]`, admitted by `exactKeys` over `Reflect.ownKeys` — a fourth key is REFUSED, never trimmed. `readApprovalIntent` additionally pins decision to the closed {APPROVE,REJECT} set and refuses an empty-string reason.

DERIVED, NEVER ACCEPTED: exactRevisionHash <- run `submissionHash`; planQualityAssessmentRef <- `state.sealedHashes.qualityHash`; criteriaRef <- the `PlanningAuthorityBodiesSealed` payload's `criteriaDigest`, SELECTED BY TYPE not index (bodies and envelope share the aggregate and write order is unpinned); goalRef and graphRevisionRef off the run; approvalRef server-minted as `approval:<runId>`. The caller cannot name a revision at all, which makes a diverged ref UNREPRESENTABLE here rather than merely refused — the seam is stronger than the shipped path on that axis, recorded because it makes APPROVAL_GRAPH_REVISION_DIVERGED unreachable from this kind by construction.

AUTHORITY COMPOSED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED: `operatorReviewAuthority` is the same composition as daemon-command-graph-approve.ts:68-79 and planning-services.ts:190-202, routed through `decideApprovalAuthority` (gate first by construction). `checkHumanAuthority` is NOT called anywhere — it is unpublished from the core barrel by design.

A DEFECT MY OWN ARM CAUGHT, and it is worth the record. First run was 15/16: the not-PLAN_REVIEW arm got BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING because I read the sealed facts BEFORE the lifecycle, so a merely-proposed run answered UNSEALED — exactly the mis-naming `approval-run-binding.ts:135-142` warns about ("answering 'unsealed' for it would name the wrong defect to the operator"). Fixed by calling `verifyApprovedRunBinding` first and forwarding its code AND layer. The arm's own fixture was also wrong: `driveThrough(store,"plan.propose")` stops at the FIRST kind match and leaves no run at all, so the arm would have been satisfied by the missing-run answer and never exercised the lifecycle check. It now drives `bootstrapSequence()` by commandId up to `cmd-finalize` and ASSERTS the subject exists and is short of PLAN_REVIEW before dispatching.

TYPE SAFETY: `ApprovalIntentRefused.layer` is typed as the closed `ServiceRefusedBy` roster, not `string` — that is the compile-time agreement check between whatever answered and what `refuse` accepts. No `any`, no `as never` (an interim `as never` was removed in favour of the real type).

ONE TRACKED EDIT so far: `bootstrap-ledger.ts` SERVICE_REFUSED_BY gains the literal `"DAEMON_APPROVAL_INTENT"`. The layer const stays module-private and only the closed TYPE is exported — the precedent APPROVAL_RUN_BINDING and the budget pair follow, and it keeps `tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts` from demanding a hostile trio for a name that only tags a composition refusal.

NOT TOUCHED, as step 3 requires: `daemon-command-graph-approve.ts` and `planning-services.ts` (the latter also carries a foreign one-line hunk). No Control Room file; DEV_PAYLOADS untouched.

LINE CAPS: approval-intent.ts 201, approval-intent-sources.ts 146 — both under the 250 target. Test file 345 (not held to the production cap).

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 4 — WIRE IT, AND CARRY THE ROSTER FAN-OUT IN THE SAME COMMIT.

Wire the seam per step 1(c)'s recorded decision — either narrowing `approval.decide`'s PAYLOAD_KEYS or registering the new kind — across `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts`, `daemon-command-families.ts` and `daemon-command-registry.ts`.

EVERY EXACT-ROSTER ASSERTION THE CHANGE REACHES MOVES IN THIS COMMIT. A commit that lands a roster change without its count consumers leaves the daemon suite red for everyone on a shared branch. Enumerate them with `git grep -l` before editing — `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` and `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` are already owned; if the grep finds a third, name it in the step note and add it, because an exact-count assertion changing when the roster changes is the assertion working, not a scope breach (Rail 8(A)).

IF STEP 1(c) CHOSE A NEW KIND, Rail 7B binds and DoD-4 is explicit: every generated artifact and digest mirror is an OWNED PATH and is REGENERATED by its generator, never hand-edited, in the SAME commit, and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test` passes with a nonzero count. A hand-edited generated file is worse than an unregistered kind because it passes review while diverging from its source. IF STEP 1(c) CHOSE REUSE, a row comment must state that no new kind was introduced and why, per DoD-4's second clause.

THE BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER GUARD: assert every ADVERTISED kind is SERVED and every SERVED kind is ADVERTISED, deriving the served set from the registry's own dispatch composition rather than from the roster constant. A test iterating the roster alone sees only one direction — deleting an entry shrinks its own iteration and stays green.

Re-run step 2: ALL arms green, including (2) — caller-supplied `activation` or `record` is now refused on the production path. Quote the count line.

STEP 5 — DRILLS, GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE HANDOFF.

RESTORE PROTOCOL: the vocabulary, families, registry and test files are TRACKED, so `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` is valid — check `git status --porcelain` per path FIRST since they carry your edits during drills. The three new `approval-intent` files are UNTRACKED until commit and `git diff` is BLIND to them; back those to `%TEMP%/6646f888-<workerId>/` and prove restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore (64 hex, non-empty, equal). Confirm each mutation LANDED before rerunning; a silent no-op write reads as green.
D1 HONOUR A CALLER `activation` (DoD-5's named drill) -> the caller-authority refusal arm MUST red. This is the row's central property: human authority is not delegable.
D2 HONOUR A CALLER `record` -> the same class of arm reds. Run it SEPARATELY from D1 — one degree of freedom each — because a seam might fence one and not the other.
